recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a future work-group decision broadens the general canonical-fragment rules beyond contained-resource targets.
issue_request: FHIR-26666 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked the Canonical URLs section to add a nearby forward pointer explaining that canonical references can include a # fragment to identify a contained resource, because the existing text could otherwise imply that canonical always points only to the resource url element.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit 387e1b4439bd8ef4c43c586897f6df02b0a5fd81, which inserted the contained-resource exception note in source/references.html immediately after the first canonical ValueSet example. A later editorial commit corrected the possessive in that note without changing its meaning.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2020-07-13 confirm the intended forward pointer. The current source also has a detailed Canonical Reference and Fragments section with full-canonical and fragment-only contained ValueSet examples. The Jira comment about Questionnaire.item.definition does not require a broader canonical datatype edit because that element is typed uri and separately documents StructureDefinition/ElementDefinition fragment use. The companion FHIR-26667 contained-reference clarification is already audited on the combined branch, and later Requirements issue FHIR-47736 handled statement references separately without changing this rule.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the build source already satisfies the Jira request and no current source correction is needed.
